findings.quote: if it falls **outside** the edge and nothing holds the object, gravity turns it farther over and it tips.
findings.problem: The lesson defines the base using points currently touching the support. A box tilted slightly about one bottom edge touches the floor only along that edge. Its weight line falls outside that contact region, but gravity restores the box upright. Being outside the current contact region does not establish that gravity turns it farther over. The direction depends on which side of the pivot the weight line occupies.
findings.source: [OpenStax College Physics, Section 9.3, Figures 9.11–9.12](https://openstax.org/books/college-physics/pages/9-3-stability), showing restoring torque for a small tilt and overturning torque after the weight line crosses the pivot.
